A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LaMP and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably across the appendix expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation, retrieval, and captioning results, component ablations, and qualitative outputs in Tables 1–6 and the main-text and appendix figures.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a transfer experiment, inference-time measurements, and illustrated failure cases in Appendix A.4–A.6.

M1.justification: The four pretraining objectives, motion-generation procedure, retrieval model, and LoRA-based captioner are unchanged. The new VQ-VAE description and Figure A1 disclose architecture details without establishing a change to the method.

E1.justification: HumanML3D, KIT-ML, and the three principal tasks are retained. Appendix A.6 adds an illustrated unseen-action scenario involving a person flying. The transfer experiment reuses existing datasets; MoCap is discussed as prior work, not used for evaluation.

E2.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their comparator sets. The new timing plot uses existing generation baselines, including MoMask and T2M-GPT. DLP and HumanTomato are discussed but not evaluated. Table 1's TM24T-to-TM2T edit corrects the name of the same cited comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 introduces a protocol using HumanML3D-pretrained LaMP while retraining motion generation on KIT-ML. Appendix A.5 adds average inference time over 100 samples on one NVIDIA 2080Ti. The existing benchmark splits, metrics, and experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostics beyond the retained component ablations and successful examples. New analyses examine transfer between datasets, generation quality versus inference cost, and failures involving erroneous annotations and unseen motions (Table A1 and Figures A3–A5).

E5.justification: Table A1 continues the existing plus/minus reporting practice. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, or the meaning of those uncertainty terms, and v2 adds no significance testing. The 100 timing samples specify an evaluation workload, not repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises DiverseMotion's HumanML3D scores, including Top-1 R-Precision from 0.510 to 0.496 and FID from 0.103 to 0.070. Table A1 newly reports transfer FID 0.226 versus 0.141 with KIT-ML pretraining; Figure A3 reports LaMP inference time of 0.08 seconds. Failure examples are also added. LaMP's main benchmark scores and Tables 2–6 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the attention-rank argument in Section 3.2.2, and the appendix's quantization and loss formulations are retained. No new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about language-motion alignment, autoregressive masked generation, retrieval, captioning, and LaMP-BertScore. The headline FID improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4–A.6 interprets the transfer results as limited generalization, attributes the timing advantage to avoiding MoMask's residual refinement, and identifies annotation errors and missing nonhuman motions as failure sources. These add substantive applicability qualifications without revising the main conclusions.

D1.justification: v2 documents VQ-VAE ReLU activations, stride-2 downsampling, nearest-neighbor upsampling, and timing hardware. Section 4.1 fills in CFG scale 4, already stated in v1 Section 3.5. A project-page link replaces the promised code-release sentence; the PDFs do not establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to DLP and HumanTomato. Section 2 and new Appendix A.7 explain differences concerning captioning instruction tuning, encoder architecture, and alignment objectives. This is a targeted expansion of positioning; the central novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains verbatim, with localized wording, typo, and affiliation edits. The appendix gains Sections A.4–A.7, while the existing qualitative-results discussion becomes A.8. There is no extensive rewrite of the main narrative.

P2.justification: The appendix gains a substantial set of displays: the VQ-VAE schematic, transfer-results table, timing-quality plot, and two failure-case figures. Earlier Figures 5–8 are retained as A2 and A6–A8. Main figures and table structures remain stable, with additional title styling, conference headers, and text reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a more informative and balanced assessment by supplementing v1's ablations and successful examples with transfer measurements, runtime evidence, and explicit failures (A.4–A.6). Added architecture details and targeted prior-work discussion also improve clarity. These are useful, limited gains in transparency and practical assessment; the core method and principal empirical evidence remain unchanged.
